Zionists approach anti-genocide protesters who were standing with Palestinian flags as part of a picket against the NYT for its role in israel’s ongoing genocide of Palestinians in Gaza. The protesters repeatedly ask the Zionists to keep moving but they ignore the requests.
In its “reporting” on Palestine-“israel,” when has the NYT properly mentioned the crucial fact that 80% of Gaza’s Palestinians are stateless refugees and have been so for decades? They are Palestinians and their children and grandchildren who were robbed and expelled from their homes in what is now “israel” on the basis that they are not jewish by western-superpower-backed European Zionists in 1947/48 and later years. Today, there are 8 million Palestinian refugees in Gaza, the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, and elsewhere. Six million of them are registered in the United Nations as refugees. Their right of return to their stolen homes in what is now “israel” is enshrined in international law and UNGA 194. Their robber “israel” has obstructed their right of return for decades on the basis that they are not Jewish. The NYT understands that this colossal injustice is at the heart of what the (toilet) paper of record calls “the conflict.” But instead of properly including this in its “reporting,” NYT, in a leaked 2024 internal memo, instructs its journalists to avoid using the word Palestine and Palestinian “refugee camps,” which are camps that house stateless Palestinian refugees in extremely difficult conditions in Gaza, the West Bank, and areas outside historical Palestine. Again, these refugees are registered in the UN’s UNRWA as refugees. They carry refugee ID cards issued by a UN agency. NYT wants to erase them in order to continue to cover up israel’s heinous, decades-long crimes against Palestinians. This is just one of countless acts of egregious journalistic malpractice the Zionist paper has done for many years. Unsubscribe from NYT. For honest reporting on Palestine, follow @electronicintifada @mondoweiss @middleeastmonitor to name a few. #justiceforpalestine #nyt
